 8. It will appear from the defense pleading as stated above that the defense case is that this is a monthly tenancy although in paragraph 6 sub-paragraphs (f) and (h) it has been stated that it was for manufacturing purposes but nowhere it has been averred that it was a yearly lease and the notice required for termination of such a lease was 6 months’ notice under section 106 of the Act. It has, of course, been asserted that although rent is payable according to the English Calendar month, the monthly tenancy is not according to English Calendar month but is to commence from the 7th day of every English Calendar month presumably because the Kabuliyat was executed on the 7th April, 1940. 

 13. Mr. S. R. Paul, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellants has submitted at the outset—I think rightly—that he is not going to contend that printing and publishing business is a kind of manufacturing business but that he will contend that both the Courts below have erred in law in misconstruing the Kabuliyat Ext. 1 and failing to hold that the purpose of the lease was also type foundry business, which was a manufacturing purpose. Mr. Paul has tried to show by reference to the terms of the contract as embodied in said Kabuliyat ,that the purpose deducible from the said terms of the contract is a manufacturing on e and the learned Advocate has laid much stress on the word ‘ইত্যাদি’ used in term No. 2 of the Kabuliyat. But, as it has been pointed out by the learned Subordinate Judge, if the language used in this term No. 2 of the Kabuliyat is scrutinized, it will appear that the word ‘ইত্যাদি’ has not been used at all in stating the kinds of things which the lessee would be permitted to do on the premises in question. In that term the defendants' predecessor actually said that he would not set up the printing machine etc. in the main building, but he would construct a C. I. sheet but on the vacant space at his own costs and set up a printing machine in the said hut, 'et'c (‘ইত্যাদি’) has been used in connection with the things which the lessee was not permitted to do but not in connection with the things which the lessee was allowed to do in the premises. Of course, I do not think that much difference could have been made by repeating the word ‘ইত্যাদি’ in the second sentence also, because by applying the 'ejusdem generis rule, the word ‘ইত্যাদি’ should connote things of the same kind or nature as the preceding word i.e. ‘ছাপার মেসিন’, and it requires too much stretching of imagination to think that the parties to the Kabuliyat Ext. 1 conceived at the time of execution of the said deed that the word ‘ইত্যাদি’ should cover type-foundry business as well.
